pairs.why: preparing a place to sit: 1961, an airman squaring rows of chairs for an audience not yet there; 1944, a woman adjusting a typing chair for herself. Recognizable alignment on the bend at the chair.
she has finished: she is sitting. He has walked out of frame and the chairs stay empty. Same gesture, different ending.
lighting a fire and working an oven. Iraq 1951 has no spoken sound at all; the American kitchen film talks the whole way through about productivity. That inequality is left audible.
wider on both: another person is standing by the wall in one; a man is being served at a table in the other.
sweeping: a shopfront in a 1951 town promotion film; a stone floor in a 1957 film about a Spanish village.
the resemblance fails at the outcome: he has stopped and is leaning on the broom; she throws water down a row-house street while a voice asks what they imagine they can make out of this.
